subject: Career
title: Legacy Power: What You Leave Behind
description: A short lesson to help you apply Legacy Power: What You Leave Behind.

hook.text: She left the company two years ago. People still say: 'What would Sarah do?' That's legacy power.

buildup.text: Legacy power is influence that persists after your formal authority ends. It lives in culture, systems, and stories.

discovery.text: People with legacy power built systems, mentored successors, and embedded values into how the team operates.

twist.text: You build legacy power not in your final days but through years of consistent, principled behavior.

climax.text: Ask: 'When I leave this role, what will remain?' If the answer is 'nothing,' your power was only positional.

punchline.text: Real power outlasts your title. Build something that stays.

quiz.question: What is legacy power?
options: Influence that persists after your formal authority ends

details.summary: Legacy power is the influence that outlasts your tenure in a role, built through mentoring successors, creating lasting systems, and shaping organizational culture. It is the highest form of professional impact because it multiplies beyond your direct presence.
details.whyItMatters: Careers focused solely on personal advancement leave nothing behind. Legacy-oriented professionals create compounding positive impact that benefits organizations and individuals for years.
takeaways: Mentor successors to extend your influence beyond your tenure
Build systems and processes that outlast any individual contributor
The most enduring legacies come from developing other leaders

faq.question: At what career stage should you start thinking about your professional legacy?
faq.answer: Start in mid-career by mentoring junior colleagues and building sustainable systems. Legacy is not just a retirement concept. The actions you take at every stage accumulate into the impact you leave, and starting earlier means a larger and more meaningful legacy.

faq.question: How is legacy power different from simply having a good reputation?
faq.answer: Reputation is how people perceive you while you are present. Legacy power is the tangible impact that continues after you leave. A good reputation fades over time; a strong legacy, such as a mentored leader or a system you built, continues producing results indefinitely.
